stem: Your innate and adaptive immune systems work together. Which statement is TRUE about how they differ?

options.A: Innate is fast and the same response every time; adaptive is slower but specific and develops memory.
options.B: Innate fights bacteria; adaptive fights viruses.
options.C: Innate is for children; adaptive develops in adults.
options.D: Innate uses antibodies; adaptive uses physical barriers.

stem: What is the main role of B cells in adaptive immunity?

options.A: Produce antibodies that bind to specific pathogens.

stem: How does a vaccine protect you from a disease without making you sick?

options.A: It kills the pathogen in advance, so there's nothing left to infect you later.
options.B: It introduces an antigen (not an active pathogen) that trains your B and T cells to recognize the real pathogen later.
options.C: It boosts your innate immune system so you're permanently more resistant.
options.D: It contains antibiotics that act as a long-lasting prophylactic.

stem: The flu vaccine teaches your body to make antibodies. The genetic instructions for those antibodies travel which way?
Your immune cells multiply rapidly when fighting an infection. That rapid cell division requires a lot of energy. Where in the cell is most of the cell's ATP produced?

options.A: In the nucleus, alongside DNA replication
options.B: On the inner mitochondrial membrane, by the electron transport chain
options.C: In the cytoplasm, by glycolysis alone
options.D: In the ribosomes during protein synthesis
